title: Primary-source novelty audit of the audited RPCD route
objective: Audit whether the exact candidate statement selected by one real harness-validated T144 run, its constants, and its C050 transfer are already known, direct corollaries, or plausibly new. This task audits novelty and priority only: proof correctness is a separate T144/T145 evidence chain, and a novelty finding cannot repair or validate a proof.
acceptance_checks: Consumes the harness-injected result from a real validated T144 run and records its repository-relative path, run_id, worker, candidate statement, assumptions, constants, and statement hash; no dynamic runs/... path appears in inputs.
Fixes the exact candidate lemma and the claimed C050 corollary before searching, so similarity cannot cause the statement to drift.
Records an as-of date, databases, exact queries, spelling variants, backward references, forward citations, and negative searches in search_log.json.

Opens and checks primary papers rather than relying on snippets, secondary summaries, or memory; each source entry gives URL, version or date, theorem number, exact assumptions, constants, and the claim it supports.

Separately classifies the candidate lemma, proof technique, constant, finite-time bridge, and full C050 conclusion as known, direct corollary, apparently new within the audited search, or inconclusive.
Explicitly states that proof correctness does not establish novelty and novelty does not establish correctness; T144 hostile audit and T145 fresh reconstruction remain independent gates.
Failure of a route lemma or discovery of a prior stronger theorem is recorded as a route or priority verdict, never as a refutation of C050.
The result does not exceed E2, does not claim first discovery from absence of a hit, and preserves unresolved terminology, language, date-range, and citation-coverage gaps.

denylist: priority claims copied from model memory
search-result snippets without the underlying primary source

required_differences: Search separately for the exact statement, method family, and finite-time consequence.
Trace citations both backward from the candidate's ingredients and forward from the closest RPCD sources.
Audit constants and quantifiers rather than matching only keywords.
forbidden_methods: treating mathematical correctness as evidence of novelty
treating novelty as evidence of mathematical correctness
claiming priority from memory or search snippets
reporting a failed sufficient route lemma as refutation of C050
required_controls: forward citations of arXiv:2505.23152 and its published version
random-permutation coordinate descent and Gauss-Seidel terminology variants
finite-time expected-distance versus asymptotic covariance-rate distinctions
adjacent matrix-product, non-normal transient, and without-replacement literatures
